name: Meraioth
overview: Meraioth was a male Levite and an Aaronic priest descended through Eleazar, serving within the tribe set apart for priestly duties. He is specifically noted as the father of Amariah, highlighting his place in the priestly lineage. His role as a Levite emphasizes his dedication to the service of God according to the Old Testament priestly order.
namesAndTitles: The name Meraioth means 'rebellious,' a proper name not given directly by God. This meaning may reflect a historical or familial context but is not expanded upon in Scripture. No additional titles are recorded for him.
familyAndRelationships: Meraioth is recorded as the father of Amariah, establishing a direct paternal link within the priestly genealogy. He is also inferred to be the father of Zerahiah, further situating him within the Levitical family line. Beyond these relationships, Scripture does not provide additional family details.
scriptureSignificance: Meraioth's significance lies in his position within the Aaronic priesthood, tracing his lineage through Eleazar, which affirms the continuity of priestly service in Israel. His mention in the genealogies underscores the faithfulness of God's covenant with the tribe of Levi and the maintenance of sacred duties in worship. As the father of Amariah, he contributes to the heritage of priestly leadership recorded in 1 Chronicles.
